causes.text: The Costco Teamsters union authorized a strike while negotiating a new contract, pressing for higher wages and improved benefits for the retailer's warehouse workers. The union vote increased pressure on Costco's management to reach an agreement.

source_info.title: Costco raises pay above $30 an hour for many, as Teamsters union threatens strike

effects.text: In March 2025, Costco's new employee agreement increased the top-of-scale hourly wage by roughly $1 to $31.90 and raised the minimum wage to $20. CFO Gary Millerchip said this wage hike would be a headwind for selling, general and administrative costs, but the company planned to offset the impact through productivity gains and other efficiencies.

source_info.title: Costco CFO says 50 cent wage increase poses expense ‘headwind'

causal_reasoning_chain.description: During contract talks in early 2025, the Teamsters union representing Costco warehouse workers authorized a strike, signaling willingness to walk out if wage demands were not met. The looming strike threatened to disrupt operations and tarnish Costco's reputation.

Facing this pressure, Costco negotiated a new agreement that raised entry-level pay to $20 per hour and increased top-of-scale wages by about $1, aiming to avert a strike and maintain a motivated workforce.
On 2025-03-10, management acknowledged the wage increases would pressure SG&A, and COST edged lower around the update; by week's end, the shares were down about 1%.

rationale: A credible strike threat increased labor bargaining power, compelling Costco to lift wages; management subsequently flagged the cost headwind.
counterfactual_analysis: Absent the strike authorization, Costco might have negotiated smaller raises and avoided part of the SG&A headwind.

adversarial_confounders.text: Tight labor markets and competition for retail workers could have driven wage increases regardless of union pressure.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Complicates attribution of the pay raise solely to the strike threat.

details.commentary: The Teamsters' strike authorization showed that organized labor at Costco could credibly threaten disruption to secure better terms. This higher supplier leverage translated into a richer wage and benefit package, raising Costco's structural labor cost base in its U.S. operations.

details.pestel_factor: Social - Stronger worker activism and focus on frontline pay and benefits
details.commentary: Public attention to essential workers and living wages increased expectations for retailers to share more of their profits with staff. In this social climate, Costco faced pressure to agree to a more generous contract, accepting near-term cost headwinds to preserve its reputation and employee relations.

Higher guaranteed pay raises Costco's SG&A, but can also support lower turnover and better service over time. Those operational improvements help offset some of the wage inflation, creating a balancing dynamic between labor costs and productivity gains in future periods.
